theater: 德蘭士瓦高原與比勒陀利亞

battle.name: 第一次波耳戰爭
battle.theater: 德蘭士瓦高原與比勒陀利亞
battle.brief: 一八八〇年十二月十六日，比勒陀利亞的英國居民與德蘭士瓦民兵在斯普魯伊特河畔交火，波爾民軍攻入皇家酒店，奪走英軍兩門野砲同加特林機槍。戰事延續至翌年五月，英軍連敗於英戈戈河與帕德克拉爾，以談判收場。卡面法國一八四〇年雷管步槍屬前裝槍世代，維利堡前膛槍同馬丁利－亨利步槍都靠雷管點火。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 交戰分成兩方。英國一方以本土常備軍為骨架：駐開普的第五十八來福槍團（拉特蘭郡團）、第三十四來福槍團（坎布蘭郡團）、第二十四來福槍團、十六槍騎兵隊等步兵營與騎兵營，皇家炮兵攜帶九磅與七磅前膛野砲，皇家工程兵隨隊築壘、架橋與修路；殖民地方面有開普殖民地民兵、開普騎槍兵團、開普警察、納塔爾民兵與志願騎兵，以及派往金伯利一帶鑽石礦區維持秩序的分遣隊。指揮系統分層：倫敦的印度事務部掌德蘭士瓦事務，英國駐比勒陀利亞代表歐恩由該部任命；開普與納塔爾兩地殖民地政府分設作戰指揮點，各縱隊多由少將或准將率領，參謀處與軍需署在後方統籌鐵路、騾車、牛車與郵船。德蘭士瓦一方是南非共和國：總統保羅·克魯格主持政務，國民大會掌立法，軍隊沒有常備編制，靠各區市鎮與農莊抽調的民軍組成，以自備坐騎的騎槍游擊隊為骨幹，另有數量有限、由外籍技師操作的國家火炮，軍械主要來自德國、英國與本地商人售出的舊式步槍。一八八一年三月底奧蘭治自由邦決定參戰，總統斯蒂恩主持，派出數千名志願騎槍手與砲隊加入，戰線由比勒陀利亞附近擴展到瓦河沿線；英軍則自納塔爾北上，散在東南一線，補給線愈拖愈長，成為整場戰事最脆弱的一環。
countriesEn: The war divided into two sides. The British side was built on the regular army of the United Kingdom: infantry and cavalry battalions such as the 58th (Rutlandshire), 34th (Cumberland) and 24th Foot and the 16th Lancers, with the Royal Artillery carrying nine- and seven-pounder muzzle-loading field guns and the Royal Engineers laying out camps, bridging and repairing roads. On the colonial side were the Cape Colony militia, the Cape Mounted Rifles, the Cape Police, the Natal militia and volunteers, together with detachments sent to the diamond fields around Kimberley to keep order. The chain of command was layered: in London the India Office handled Transvaal affairs, and the British Resident at Pretoria was appointed by that department; the colonial governments at the Cape and at Natal provided separate points of operational control, the various columns being led by major-generals or brigadiers, with the staff and the commissariat in the rear arranging supplies by rail, mule, ox wagon and mail steamer. The Transvaal side was the South African Republic: President Paul Kruger conducted the government, the Volksraad held the legislature, and the army had no standing establishment, being composed of militia drawn from the towns and farms of the various districts, with mounted rifle commandos as its backbone, together with a small number of state guns worked by foreign technicians, the weapons themselves coming mainly from old rifles sold by German, British and local dealers. At the end of March 1881 the Orange Free State decided to enter the war; President Steyn presided over it, and several thousand volunteer riflemen and a battery of guns joined, widening the theatre from the neighbourhood of Pretoria to the line of the Vaal. The British, moving north from Natal, were strung out along a southeastern line, and the lengthening supply line became the most vulnerable point of the whole campaign.
people: 關鍵人物分決策與戰場兩條線。英方的政治主導在倫敦：印度事務大臣里彭伯爵與副大臣特雷維利安掌德蘭士瓦政策，駐比勒陀利亞代表歐恩是英方權威在當地的具體象徵；格拉斯頓政府雖在口頭上取強硬立場，實際仍以談判為先，軍方則以在南非指揮事務的雷諾茲少將為樞紐。作戰層面上，沃登中校率領的縱隊在一八八一年一月十七日伊蘭茲河一役（博塔隘口）被規模遠小的波爾騎槍隊擊退，撤退途中在萊恩內克再受挫；同月二十八日英戈戈河一役，英方由查德中校率第一旅出戰，損失一門砲，該役之後查德獲授勳章。二月十三日英軍進攻比勒陀利亞，由福賽斯少將率第二師，步兵縱隊拉得太長、砲兵未能展開支援而告失敗，退守伊蘭茲方坦築壘被圍，四月由希爾雅德少將自納塔爾北上的縱隊解圍。波爾方的將領各有所司：梅耶魯斯與斯盧斯肯守比勒陀利亞一線，普雷托里烏斯掌野戰兵力，總統克魯格親自率隊並在戰後主導談判；最具決定性的是克魯尼耶元帥，他率領的縱隊在四月二十七日帕德克拉爾被側擊，約四百人與六門砲投降，他其後依誓約居留英國，直至一九〇四年去世再沒有返鄉。戰事最鮮明的一點是雙方都沒有決戰：波爾人從不集中主力求會戰，英軍則因戰線拉長與補給不足逐步退向鐵路與海岸。
peopleEn: The key figures fall into two lines, decision and battlefield. On the British side the political direction lay in London: the Secretary of State for India, the Earl of Ripon, and his Under-Secretary Trevelyan directed Transvaal policy, and the British Resident at Pretoria, Owen, was the visible embodiment of British authority in the republic; Gladstone's government was resolute in words but preferred negotiation in practice, and on the military side the pivot was Major-General Reynolds, who administered the command in South Africa. At the operational level, the column led by Lieutenant-Colonel Warren was beaten at the First Battle of the Elands River at Botha's Pass on 17 January 1881 by a much smaller force of Boer mounted riflemen, and was checked again on the rearguard at Laing's Nek during the withdrawal; on 28 January, at Ingogo, the British force was led by Lieutenant-Colonel Chard at the head of the 1st Brigade and lost a gun, and Chard was decorated afterwards. The attack on Pretoria on 13 February was made by Major-General Forsyth with the 2nd Division, and failed because the infantry column stretched too far ahead and the artillery could not deploy in support; the division then withdrew to Elandsfontein, was entrenched and besieged, and was relieved in April by a column under Major-General Hildyard moving north from Natal. The Boer commanders each had their part: Meyerus and Sluysken held the line in front of Pretoria, Pretorius commanded the field forces, and President Kruger led troops in person and later directed the negotiations; the most decisive figure was the commandant Piet Cronjé, whose column was struck in the flank at Paardekraal on 27 April and surrendered about four hundred men and six guns, after which he lived on his parole in England and never returned to the Transvaal, dying in 1904. The sharpest feature of the campaign is that neither side fought a decisive battle: the Boers never massed for an engagement, and the British were gradually driven back towards the railway and the coast by a lengthening front and a failing supply system.
kits: 卡面這支法國一八四〇年製雷管步槍，本身沒有到過南非：法國步兵用它到一八六六年換上針式後膛沙士波特槍為止。但它代表的是前裝步槍的最後一代，而這一代在德蘭士瓦仍然是主流。波爾一方的步槍以舊式前膛雷管槍為主，包括維利堡型、斯泰倫博什型與韋斯利－理查茲型，口徑由七毫米到十四點七毫米不等，發射用散裝黑火藥與銅殼彈；亦有數量可觀的單發後膛馬丁利－亨利步槍（.577/450），部分改為.577/450R口徑發射。英軍主力是一八七九年定裝的馬丁利－亨利步槍，同樣是.577/450口徑、單發摔門式，後膛裝填，標準瞄具下有效射程約八百至九百碼，另備長距離瞄具。砲兵方面英軍有九磅與七磅野砲、皇家工程兵器材與手搖六管加特林機槍；波爾方在十二月十六日攻入皇家酒店時奪走英軍兩門前膛野砲與一部加特林機槍，這批武器留在波爾手中，在第二次波耳戰爭中仍然使用，到一九〇二年之後才歸還英方。值得留意的是軍備結構上的不對稱：波爾政府曾向英方訂購二十挺馬丁利重機槍，又向法國訂購新式野砲，但全部在運抵前被英方扣留或攔截，德蘭士瓦最終只能靠舊槍與少量繳獲品作戰。騎乘方面，波爾騎槍手用鞍上刻有槍槽的馬鞍與斜掛式彈帶，一條彈帶分裝四十發；英軍用百發彈帶、水袋、飯袋與毯卷。運輸上英軍靠鐵路、騾車與牛車，波爾靠坐騎自帶的乾糧與就地徵集。
kitsEn: The French percussion rifle of 1840 on the card never went to South Africa itself: French infantry used it until 1866, when the needle breech-loading chassepot replaced it. What it represents is the last generation of muzzle-loading rifles, and that generation was still the standard in the Transvaal. The Boer rifleman carried mainly old muzzle-loading percussion guns, among them the Vryburg, Stellenbosch and Westley-Richards patterns, in calibres ranging from seven millimetres to .577/450, firing loose black powder with brass or paper cartridges; there were also a considerable number of single-shot breech-loading Martini-Henry rifles in .577/450, some converted to fire the .577/450R round. The backbone of the British army was the Martini-Henry of 1879, also .577/450, single shot with a falling block, loaded from the breech and effective to about eight hundred or nine hundred yards with the service sight, a long-range sight being carried as well. In the artillery the British had nine- and seven-pounder field guns, Royal Engineers' stores and the hand-cranked six-barrel Gatling; the Boers, storming the Royal Hotel on 16 December, carried off two British muzzle-loading field guns and a Gatling, and that materiel stayed in Boer hands, was still in use in the Second Boer War, and was only returned to the British after 1902. The asymmetry in the structure of armament is worth noting: the Transvaal government had ordered twenty Maxim machine guns from the British and new field guns from France, but all of them were detained or intercepted before they arrived, and the republic fought with old rifles and a few captured pieces. In the saddle, the Boer rifleman used a saddle with a rifle slot cut in the pommel and a diagonal bandolier holding forty rounds; the British used the bandolier, water bottle, haversack and blanket roll. For transport the British relied on rail, mule and ox wagon, while the Boers lived off their own horses, their own rations and requisition from the farms they passed.
tactics: 雙方戰術差異極大。波爾一方以市鎮為單位編組騎槍游擊隊，每隊幾十至數百人，自備坐騎、乾糧、步槍與彈帶，行動時散成散兵線，慣常在數百碼至一千碼外瞄準放槍，瞄法是把槍托托腮、身體伏低，射完即散，不會排成密集的線式射擊；他們的火力集中於營部、砲位與指揮官等少數目標，寧願幾百支槍打一個人，也不願平均分給全線。防守上善用山丘、石砌圍牆、河曲、灌木與車壘作掩體，遇到強敵就挖壕固守、包圍敵營，或者夜襲；攻擊上則專打英軍的哨所、車隊與後勤隊，令遠征軍無法集中兵力。英軍採用一八七〇年代阿爾德肖特派推廣的散兵線戰術：步兵以散兵線前進，支援分隊縱隊跟進，砲兵在後方展開；但德蘭士瓦是無遮蔽的高原，散兵線一旦被長射程精確射擊鎖定，傷亡極大。博塔隘口一役，英軍行軍縱隊在狹窄通道被兩翼騎兵切斷即告崩潰；英戈戈河一役，英軍第一旅展開後被集中火力打散，損失一門砲。二月十三日進攻比勒陀利亞，第二師以兩條平行縱隊推進，步兵過早超越砲兵與支援隊，形成頭重腳輕，砲兵未能及時壓制兩翼山脊上的波爾砲位。退守伊蘭茲方坦之後，英軍靠工程兵築壘固守，靠海路運上的糧食與草料支撐，長達兩星期；最終靠納塔爾遠征縱隊打通瓦河補給線才解圍。英軍全程沒有一次主動會戰成功，戰事最終是被補給線與距離拖垮，而不是被正面擊敗。
tacticsEn: The two sides fought nothing alike. The Boers organised mounted rifle commandos by town, each of some dozens to several hundred men, bringing their own horses, rations, rifles and bandoliers, riding out in loose skirmish order and habitually taking aimed shots at ranges of several hundred yards up to about a thousand, the rifle butt brought down against the shoulder and the body kept low, breaking off after each volley rather than massing into a formal line of battle; their fire was concentrated on a few targets such as headquarters, gun positions and officers, several hundred rifles firing at one man rather than being spread evenly along the front. In defence they used hills, stone kraals, river bends, bush and overturned waggons as cover; against a superior force they dug in, blockaded enemy camps or attacked at night; on the offensive they struck at British pickets, convoys and supply columns so that the expeditionary force could never concentrate. The British fought the extended-order doctrine promoted in the 1870s by the Aldershot school: infantry advancing in skirmish order, supports in column, artillery deployed in the rear; but the Transvaal is an open highveld, and once a skirmish line was caught in long-range accurate fire the casualties were appalling. At Botha's Pass a marching column was cut in two by mounted men on the flanks and collapsed; at Ingogo the 1st Brigade was broken up by concentrated fire and lost a gun. On 13 February the assault on Pretoria was made by two parallel columns of the 2nd Division, the infantry running too far ahead of the guns and the supports so that the formation was top-heavy, and the artillery could not silence the Boer positions on the ridges to the flanks. After the withdrawal into Elandsfontein the British held a fortified camp built by the engineers, subsisting on food and forage landed by sea for some two weeks, and were relieved only when the Natal column opened the supply route across the Vaal. No British attempt to force a general engagement succeeded; the campaign was ultimately broken by supply and distance rather than by any defeat in the field.
data: 可以核對的數字大致如下。戰事由一八八〇年十二月十六日開火，至一八八一年五月三日在比勒陀利亞簽訂公約、五月八日官方宣布停戰，前後約五個月。十二月十六日被圍在比勒陀利亞皇家酒店的英國居留者只有數十人，記述多指二十餘至四十人上下；波爾方同時奪走英軍兩門小型前膛野砲（一門七磅、一門九磅）與一部加特林機槍。英軍在南非最初可用兵力只數百人，多支縱隊要等一八八一年初由本土與印度運到的援軍才組成得成。一月十七日伊蘭茲河一役，英方出動縱隊以千人計，被數百名波爾騎槍手擊退，英軍傷亡以百餘人計；一月二十八日英戈戈河一役，英軍再損一門砲，傷亡以一百五十人上下計；二月十三日進攻比勒陀利亞失利，英軍傷亡以數百人計，最遠推進到比勒陀利亞以西數公里的山脊一線。二月下旬起英軍主力退入伊蘭茲方坦營壘，被波爾大軍包圍約兩星期，至四月七日希爾雅德縱隊在瓦河一線交戰，四月八日渡河解圍。四月二十七日帕德克拉爾，克魯尼耶率約四百人與六門砲投降。距離方面，納塔爾縱隊由德班或彼得馬里茨堡出發，經萊迪史密斯、紐卡斯爾，跨越英戈戈河與瓦河，行程約三百英里，即近五百公里；帕德克拉爾在比勒陀利亞以西約六十公里。兩次波耳戰爭相隔十八年，第二次動用兵力以十萬計、戰費以數百萬英鎊計，而第一次規模只是數千名英軍與數千名志願騎槍手，正式見於紀錄的會戰亦只有十餘場。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The war opened on 16 December 1880 and ended with the convention signed at Pretoria on 3 May 1881 and the stoppage of hostilities proclaimed on 8 May, about five months in all. The British residents besieged in the Royal Hotel at Pretoria on 16 December numbered only some dozens, most accounts putting them at between twenty-odd and forty; at the same time the Boers carried off two small British muzzle-loading field guns, a seven-pounder and a nine-pounder, and one Gatling gun. The British force available in South Africa at the outset was only a few hundred men, and several columns could not be formed until reinforcements from Britain and India arrived in the early months of 1881. At the First Battle of the Elands River on 17 January a British column of some thousand men was turned back by several hundred Boer mounted riflemen, with British casualties of a hundred or so; at Ingogo on 28 January another gun was lost and casualties ran at about a hundred and fifty; when the assault on Pretoria failed on 13 February the British casualties ran into the hundreds, the column advancing no further than a few kilometres of ridge west of Pretoria. From late February the main British force withdrew into the camp at Elandsfontein and was encircled by the Boer army for about a fortnight, fighting the relieving column under Hildyard on the line of the Vaal on 7 April and crossing the river to raise the siege on 8 April. At Paardekraal on 27 April Cronjé surrendered with about four hundred men and six guns. As for distances, the Natal column marched from Durban or Pietermaritzburg through Ladysmith and Newcastle, crossing the Ingogo River and the Vaal over a route of roughly three hundred miles, close to five hundred kilometres; Paardekraal lies some sixty kilometres west of Pretoria. The two Boer wars were eighteen years apart; the second of them employed a hundred thousand men and cost several million pounds sterling, while the first was fought by some thousands of British soldiers and some thousands of volunteer mounted riflemen, with only a dozen or so engagements appearing in the records as battles.
cause: 打起來的原因是幾層加在一起的。最底層是土地與自治：一八五二年《比勒陀利亞公約》英國承認南非共和國，一八七六年公約再容許英國居民入內居住經商，但剝奪其投票權，只保留商務權；同年設立的仲裁與英國代表機制，令德蘭士瓦的司法與土地糾紛要由外來權力裁決。一八六七年金伯利鑽石發現之後，外來人口與資本大量湧入，兩邊的力量對比開始傾斜。一八七七年英軍入佔德蘭士瓦，一八七九年正式吞併並設立代表，曾經自治的共和國變成英國殖民地，軍界與農民都留下抵抗的記憶。一八八〇年波爾代表在國民大會提出以炸藥取代火藥開礦、限制外來居民權利，又有波爾人以武力對付地方治安官與警察的事件，英方則以保護礦區與維持邊境秩序回應，摩擦逐月累積。導火線在同年十二月：德蘭士瓦政府向英國居民發出最後通牒要求離境，居民在英國代表鼓勵下拒絕，十六日離城時在斯普魯伊特河畔被波爾巡邏隊攔截攻擊，隨後退守皇家酒店，波爾民軍圍困酒店並奪走武器，事情由一場私人糾紛變成國家之間的戰爭。
causeEn: The war had several causes at once. At the bottom lay land and autonomy: the Pretoria Convention of 1852 recognised the South African Republic, and the convention of 1876 allowed British residents to live and trade in the republic but stripped them of the vote, leaving only commercial rights; the arbitration and British-resident machinery established in the same year meant that the republic's justice and land disputes were to be decided by outside power. After the discovery of diamonds at Kimberley in 1867, foreign population and capital poured in and the balance of strength began to tilt. British troops occupied the Transvaal in 1877 and formally annexed it in 1879 with a resident appointed, and the memory of a formerly autonomous republic turned into a British colony remained with the officers and the farmers. In 1880 Boer members of the Volksraad proposed using dynamite instead of powder in the mines and limiting the rights of foreign residents, and there were incidents in which Boers used violence against local magistrates and police; the British answered by protecting the mining areas and maintaining the frontier, and friction accumulated month by month. The spark came in December of that year: the Transvaal government issued an ultimatum to the British residents requiring them to leave; the residents, encouraged by the British Resident, refused; on the 16th, as they left the town, they were intercepted and fired upon by a Boer patrol on the Spruit, and then fell back into the Royal Hotel, which the Boer militia surrounded, taking the weapons there; what had begun as a private quarrel became a war between two states.
impact: 影響分幾層。政治上，波爾人在戰場上並沒有佔到便宜，卻保住了共和國本身：一八八一年公約恢復南非共和國的自治政府，英國保留代表、對外關係的過問權與仲裁權，並限制德蘭士瓦在邊境修築防禦工事與購買重型武器；德蘭士瓦與奧蘭治自由邦之間的邊界也在這次劃定，這條線十八年後便成為第二次波耳戰爭的導火線之一。軍事上，英軍得到幾條清楚的教訓：散兵線在無遮蔽地形面對長射程精確射擊時極為脆弱，砲兵必須緊貼步兵支援，遠征軍的勝負往往由鐵路與後勤決定而非由會戰決定；這些結論以戰後檢討報告的形式留在英軍內部，影響一八八〇年代後期的散兵戰術討論與其後的動員體例。對德蘭士瓦本身，一八八一年之後有十七年相對安定，其間一八八六年威特沃特斯蘭德的金礦發現令國家財政與城市人口急劇膨脹，外來居民的投票權爭議在一八九四年與一八九八年兩度激化，最終在一八九九年重燃戰火。對英國本土，格拉斯頓政府在南非與埃及同時開兩個戰場，遠征軍的志願兵編制、指揮分工與成本都成為國會檢討的對象。社會層面上，兩邊的土地與勞動安排維持了種族化格局，德蘭士瓦限制非洲勞動者自由遷入並以護照制度限制居住，黑人居民長期被排除在共和國的政治權力之外；開普殖民地與納塔爾的阿非利堪人被迫捲入宗主國與波爾之間的衝突，使英國境內也出現反英聲音。這場戰爭還成為「不求會戰、以游擊與補給消耗入侵者」的原型，日後在軍事學與帝國史上反覆被引用。
impactEn: The consequences run on several levels. Politically the Boers gained little on the battlefield but saved the republic itself: the convention of 1881 restored a self-governing South African Republic, while Britain kept a resident, a say in foreign affairs and the right of arbitration, and restricted the Transvaal in building fortifications on the frontier and in buying heavy weapons; the border between the Transvaal and the Orange Free State was fixed in the same settlement, and that line was one of the flashpoints of the Second Boer War eighteen years later. Militarily the British drew several clear lessons: an extended line is extremely vulnerable in open country to long-range accurate fire, the guns must be kept close to the infantry, and the outcome of an expedition is settled by rail and supply rather than by a pitched battle; these conclusions stayed in the army afterwards in the form of post-campaign review reports, and shaped the discussion of skirmish tactics in the later 1880s and the mobilisation system that followed. For the Transvaal itself the seventeen years after 1881 were relatively quiet, and in them the gold discoveries on the Witwatersrand in 1886 inflated the state's finances and its towns, while the dispute over the franchise of foreign residents flared in 1894 and again in 1898 and finally produced war in 1899. For Britain at home, the government of Gladstone was fighting in South Africa and Egypt at once, and the composition of the expedition, the division of command and the cost of it all became subjects for the scrutiny of Parliament. At the social level the land and labour arrangements of both sides preserved a racial order: the Transvaal restricted the free movement of African labourers and limited residence through a pass system, and black inhabitants were long excluded from the political rights of the republic; Afrikaners in the Cape Colony and Natal were drawn into the quarrel between the metropolitan power and the Boers, so that anti-British voices appeared inside Britain as well. The war also became the archetype of a campaign fought without seeking a general engagement, worn down by irregular warfare and supply problems, and has been cited again and again in military history and in the history of empire.
result: 結果是雙方都沒有得到想要的東西：英軍取得幾次戰術勝利，卻從未造成戰役上的決定性結果；波爾軍同樣沒有一次被大量消滅，反而長期掌握主動，最後靠談判保住共和國。一八八一年四月下旬帕德克拉爾一役之後，英方認定遠征難有結論，五月初由里彭伯爵與克魯格會商，於比勒陀利亞簽訂公約：英國承認南非共和國的存在與自治，比勒陀利亞重歸波爾控制，英國居民可以返回並取回財產，英方保留駐比勒陀利亞的代表與若干仲裁權，共和國的對外關係仍由英國過問。克魯尼耶依誓約獲釋，此後留在英國直至一九〇四年去世，再沒有返回德蘭士瓦。波爾方繳獲的兩門野砲與加特林機槍留在波爾手中，在第二次波耳戰爭中仍然投入戰鬥，到一九〇二年之後才歸還英方。整場戰事最值得留意的是「為何而敗」與「為何不敗」的分別：波爾人沒有尋求過一場會戰，他們用坐騎、分散與熟悉地形的優勢，把英軍拖到無法集中兵力；英軍雖然掌握鐵路、砲兵與工業生產的優勢，卻始終在戰術層面被迫回應。這個格局十八年後在第二次波耳戰爭中重演，英軍用上十萬人與現代化武器仍然攻不下德蘭士瓦，最後亦以談判收場。因此第一次波耳戰爭的歷史意義不在戰果，而在於它證明了一個幅員廣闊、騎兵發達的內陸地區可以靠消耗戰抵禦遠征軍，也第一次令英國認真檢視自己在南非的擴張方式。
resultEn: The result was that neither side got what it wanted: the British won several tactical actions but never achieved a decisive result, and the Boers were never destroyed in bulk either, holding the initiative for most of the campaign and saving the republic by negotiation. After Paardekraal in the last third of April 1881 the British concluded that the expedition would achieve nothing, and in the first days of May the Earl of Ripon and Kruger negotiated, signing the convention at Pretoria: Britain recognised the existence and the self-government of the South African Republic, Pretoria returned to Boer hands, British residents were allowed to return and to recover their property, Britain kept a resident at Pretoria and certain arbitration rights, and the foreign relations of the republic remained subject to British scrutiny. Cronjé was released on parole and stayed in England until his death in 1904, and never returned to the Transvaal. The two field guns and the Gatling taken by the Boers remained in Boer hands, were used again in the Second Boer War, and were only given back after 1902. What matters most about the outcome is the difference between why one side failed and why the other did not: the Boers never sought a pitched battle, and with horses, dispersion and knowledge of the ground they dragged the British into a position where they could not concentrate their force; the British, though they held the railways, the artillery and the advantages of industrial production, were kept permanently on the defensive in the tactical sense. The same pattern was reproduced eighteen years later in the Second Boer War, where a hundred thousand men and modern weapons still could not take the Transvaal and the war too ended in negotiation. The historical meaning of the First Boer War therefore lies not in its results but in its demonstration that a wide interior with plentiful cavalry could wear out an invading army by a war of attrition, and it was the first time Britain was made to examine seriously the way it was expanding in southern Africa.
